machine.shared: A development machine, with other work running at times; the A/B runs are alternated for that reason

build.tls: OpenSSL 3.6.5 (bundled, static: linux-ext-libs 1.25); mbedTLS not built on this machine
build.note: CONFIG_DEBUG_TRACK_MEMORY is on (the .config of this machine): every allocation is tracked. A build without it does less work per allocation; that build was not measured here.

method.ab: Written on 2026-10-24, before the tag. 7.27.11 is the C code of the release: the main tree at deb4af519 (the version bump changes no C). It is measured against 7.27.10, the last release with a study. The only C change is in tr_treedb.c and c_treedb.c: the yuno in the ids of a treedb's lists, built when a treedb or a topic is opened. 7.27.10 and 7.27.11 each built from a git worktree, with the same .config and compiler; outputs_ext shared (linux-ext-libs 1.25 at both). In each tree only the kernel libraries, the modules, performance/c/ and the three ctest binaries were built; no benchmark source changed between the two. The two binaries of each benchmark run in rotation, the order turned every round, with a sync and a 3 s pause before each run (1 s for the three ctest binaries and the read phase): 8 rounds; 24 for perf_tr_treedb, perf_timeranger2, the TCP and TLS echo and both event loop echoes; 48 for the append test (the test_topic_pkey_integer chain) and for the read phase; perf_rotatory 16. The BFF logins measured -1.69% (t = -3.3) after 32 rounds of that rotation; perf_auth_bff never calls the changed functions (gdb: no breakpoint of them hit), but the change moved its hot code (event loop, gobj, llhttp, jansson) 128 bytes. A controlled re-run of 24 rounds rotated three binaries: 7.27.10, 7.27.11, and 7.27.10's code relinked with the placement of 7.27.11 (a 120-byte pad in tr_treedb.o; 17 258 of 17 926 functions at the addresses of 7.27.11): those are its figures in this report. Mean +- standard deviation (median), t = the change over its standard error; |t| < 3 is noise. The treedb figures are CPU time of the process per operation.
method.tag_run: The absolute figures of 7.27.11 are its side of the A/B run: its C code (deb4af519), built on 2026-10-24 on the machine of the earlier reports. The per-second benchmarks drop their first and last second; reads page by page are the FORWARD pass. The binary sizes are those of the yunos built from the main tree at the same commit, with the same .config.

story.title: Yuneta 7.27.11: two replicas of one treedb, two feeds
story.lead: 7.27.11 puts the yuno in the ids of a treedb's lists. A replica names a directory of the store after each id, and the id was unique inside one process only: every yuno of a realm that read the realm's authz store as a replica shared one directory, and a change could reach one of them and miss the others. The id is built when a treedb or a topic is opened, never per record. Against 7.27.10, the last release with a study, every one of the 41 figures stays inside its noise.

hero.text: figures inside their noise against 7.27.10: the fix is in the open of a treedb, not in any path that runs per record.

tiles: treedb: update a node and save it
A page of 1 row, as a replica
story.ab_sub: Each benchmark built from the tree of each release (7.27.10 and 7.27.11), the binaries run in rotation: 8 rounds, 24 for the treedb writes, the store open and the echoes, 48 for the appends and the read path, 24 for the BFF logins in a controlled three-way re-run. A change inside its whisker is noise. Everything is on one axis: the change of the time an operation takes.
story.prices_sub: What got slower, how much, in which release, and what it buys.
story.no_prices: None. The BFF logins measured -1.69% (t = -3.3) in the rotation of the study; perf_auth_bff never calls the changed code, a controlled re-run measured +0.08% (t = 0.05), and 7.27.10's code relinked with the placement of 7.27.11 measured as 7.27.11 did: code placement, not code. The treedb figures are 2-7% faster and the C_TREEDB opens 2-3.5% slower, all within their noise (|t| < 1.5): their spread is wide at 8 and 24 rounds.
story.abs_sub: Absolute figures of the 7.27.11 build (its C code: deb4af519), measured on 2026-10-24, before the tag, on the laptop above, as its side of the A/B run: one process, one core for the event loop (Yuneta scales by running one yuno per core). Mean of the rounds; the spread and the rounds are in the table at the end.
